head: working-tree
subject: HTTP/1 field-value validation uses the shared control-byte table
change: HTTP/1 had four copies of the field-value control-byte check: the streaming head scan, parseHeaderLine, validateHeaderValue, and validateReasonPhrase each compared every byte against 0x20 and 0x7f. The shared src/http/field_value.zig now exposes inline invalidByte backed by the same 256-byte table already used by HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, and all four HTTP/1 sites use it. The accepted grammar and error types are unchanged; HTTP/1 already had its own field-name table.
notes: The borrowed scenario is neutral because its measured cost is dominated by header-storage and start-line work; the value scan share is smaller there. The owned paths improved 7.8-8.5% with every pair faster. The bench-http1-parse baseline was re-recorded with the three existing entries under the unpinned cpu32 fingerprint. The host was loaded during the batch (load average roughly 10 to 30), so only interleaved ratios are claimed.
